paper.title: Evolutionary Computation for Wind Farm Layout Optimization
paper.authors: Dennis Wilson and Silvio Rodrigues and Carlos Segura and Ilya Loshchilov and Frank Hutter and Guillermo Lopez Buenfil and Ahmed Kheiri and Ed Keedwell and Mario Ocampo-Pineda and Ender Ozcan and Sergio Ivvan Valdez Pena and Brian Goldman and Salvador Botello Rionda and Arturo Hernandez-Aguirre and Kalyan Veeramachaneni and Sylvain Cussat-Blanc

paper_source_conflicts: The public archive labelled CMA-ES contains a grid fill/refinement method and no identifiable covariance-matrix adaptation, whereas the paper explicitly defines active CMA-ES over a five-variable geometric decoder.
The four released entries use different RNGs, languages, caching rules, and physical-evaluation counters.
The source-level 3s-MDE interpolated surrogate and the HPC analytic lattice aggregation have different absolute boundary calibration.
missing_information: author CMA-ES optimizer source matching the paper
completion_decisions: Compile the five public XML scenarios unchanged and independently reproduce the released C++ WindFLO equations.
Port 3s-MDE, SSHH, and Goldman from the paper plus released entry source while preserving physical-FES semantics.
Reconstruct CMA-ES from the paper's five-variable decoder and standard rank-mu covariance adaptation; do not relabel the conflicting MATLAB archive.
Use deterministic counter-keyed random events and ordered state commits rather than claim cross-language bit-stream identity.

Analytically aggregate 3s-MDE lattice pair-surrogate terms; decode exact layouts for physical evaluations and use a declared deterministic half-batch completion only if absolute surrogate calibration admits too few trials.
Flatten candidate-by-direction evaluation and use one persistent CPU team.
Run the complete four-method by five-scenario paper matrix once because the paper reports one competition result per role and no independent statistical repeats.
Request every available Waffle CPU core for every role; retain paper-ordered stateful trajectories and use independent candidate and direction parallelism.

scope.claim_boundary: academic declared reproduction of the paper problem and four main methods; not author-exact numerical or runtime reproduction

decision_variables.resolution: method-specific low-dimensional geometric or integer layout variables decoded to continuous turbine coordinates

encoding_and_decoder.resolution: rhomboid 3s-MDE, five-variable geometric CMA-ES, X-Y-S grid SSHH, and two-vector Goldman lattice

constraints_and_repair.resolution: rectangular bounds inclusive, rectangle obstacle interiors excluded, and minimum center distance 8R=308 m

wake_power_cost_or_coupled_model.resolution: Kusiak/Jensen conical wake, RSS deficits, piecewise 1.5 MW power, released capital/substation/O&M and annuity cost

wind_and_scenario_sampling.resolution: 24 15-degree sectors with per-sector Weibull scale, shape and directional density; 0.5 m/s integration from 3.5 to 14 m/s plus released rated tail

initialization.resolution: paper/source initialization for each of the four methods

update_order.resolution: parallel independent candidates and directions followed by deterministic paper-order selection, learned-sequence, covariance or coordinate commits

stopping_and_physical_fes.resolution: 2000 complete WindFLO evaluations per scenario and 10000 across five scenarios; cache and surrogate-only calls do not count

parameters.resolution: 3s-MDE Table 3, CMA-ES m0=[0.5]^5 sigma0=0.3 defaults, SSHH 1800 post-initial evaluations and released LLHs, Goldman 36 angle and 64 magnitude intervals

training_and_inference_lifecycle.resolution: online SSHH sequence learning is contained within each optimization; no offline trained model

metrics_and_repeats.resolution: energy cost, wake-free ratio, energy output, feasibility, physical FES, stage timings and scientific hash for one paper-native competition run per method/scenario; any 25-seed platform robustness extension is separate and is not an admission blocker
